schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: read_and_write() — one HTTPS GET of the account's usage (seven_day and five_hour utilization and reset times), written to one JSON file; last() — the stored reading with its age and whether the last fetch failed; python -m cairn.tools.usage [--fetch] [--json] prints it, and python -m cairn.tools.usage --hook is the Stop-hook entry that fetches, writes, and always exits 0. The fetch is injectable (fetch=) so a proof touches no network.
why: Akien, 2026-11-12 (idea 1a1994e293cb): the orchestrator has to watch usage to drive the cc_0 boxes ('could be a hook again, writing a json file that you could just look at any time you wanted to'); the old update-usage.sh fed a widget that no longer exists. One reading, one file, and a file that never passes stale data off as fresh: every answer carries fetched_at and age_s, and a failed fetch is written BESIDE the last good reading, never in its place (Law 7: a record of truth never collapses an error).
entry: BUILT 2026-11-12, ticket 6b0dfaa14efd, from idea 1a1994e293cb; the orchestrator's draft was the starting point. The endpoint's real reply shape is a HYPOTHESIS: no network call has been measured.
invoke: `python -m cairn.tools.usage` prints the last reading and its age; `--fetch` fetches first; `--json` prints the record; `--hook` is the Stop-hook entry (wiring it into settings is the operator's act, not this tool's). Store: ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/tools/usage/usage.json (override CAIRN_USAGE_FILE). Credentials: ~/.claude/.credentials.json (override CAIRN_USAGE_CREDS). The OAuth token is read to send one request and is never printed, logged or written.
state_and_history: A TOOL HOLDS NO STATE OF ITS OWN (Law 6). The reading file is cached state berthed under its holder, the cc device (outline 1.3.1, answered open-44690b1b31d8): ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/tools/usage/, instance-space, never in git.
proof: proofs/test_usage_reads_and_keeps_one_file.py — six teeth: one per falsifier clause, fetch injected and urlopen patched to raise so no network is touched, plus the default store berthing under the cc holder.
gates: Import gate — encapsulation_holds in build_inspector (RULE 1) reds any reach landing off this tool's declared module. Seal: the tester seals the proof into validations/ beside it.
falsifier: Red if a good fetch is not written with its time, if a failed fetch replaces the last good reading or reads as fresh, if the OAuth token ever appears in the store or in any output, if --hook exits non-zero, or if the proof reaches the network.
how_it_learns: It does not; it is a fixed reader — one fetch, one file.
traces_to: CP4 and Law 7 (a failed fetch is permanent in the record, never collapsed into a fresh-looking reading)
Law 3 (a usage figure is a measurement with an age, not a belief)
Law 6 (a tool has users, not an owner)
owner: None — a tool has users (Law 6): the orchestrator and any session that wants the usage figure. CC gates writes to its code and proofs.
